title: indian shares fall widening iran conflict sends oil higher 2026 09 02
text:
Sept 2 (Reuters) - Indian shares fell alongside global markets on Wednesday as renewed U.S.-Iran strikes heightened the risk of disruptions to ​oil flows, reviving inflation concerns amid a global bond rout that ‌pushed borrowing costs to multi-decade highs.
The Asian country is the third-largest crude importer and consumer, making it vulnerable to a sustained rise in oil prices, which can push up ​the cost of living, hurt growth and widen the import bill.
"Market ​sentiment remains under pressure amid a sharp surge in crude oil ⁠prices, triggered by escalating geopolitical tensions in West Asia, which has significantly ​dampened traders' risk appetite," said Sudeep Shah, head of technical and derivatives research ​at SBI Securities.
India's Nifty 50 (.NSEI)
, opens new tab
 fell 0.59% to 23,914.45 and the Sensex (.BSESN)
, opens new tab
 shed 0.49% to 76,570.35, paring losses of 0.7% and 0.6% from before the closing auction.
The indexes have fallen 5% ​since the Iran war broke out more than six months ago.
Eleven of ​the 16 major sectors declined. The broader small-caps (.NIFSMCP100)
, opens new tab
 and mid-caps (.NIFMDCP100)
, opens new tab
 lost 0.4% and 0.5%, respectively.
The ‌U.S. ⁠and Iran are back on a war footing after the most significant exchange of fire in weeks, with Washington threatening more devastating strikes.
Brent crude rose 0.3% to $95 a barrel, paring some gains after hitting a near-six-month high earlier ​in the session, lifting ​bond yields ⁠on worries of a near-term U.S. rate hike.
Higher U.S. rates make emerging markets less attractive for global investors.
Among stocks, Hero ​MotoCorp (HROM.NS)
, opens new tab
 dipped 4.6%, leading losses on the auto index (.NIFTYAUTO)
, opens new tab
, which ​fell 1.8%, ⁠after exports for India's top two-wheeler maker slid and market share declined in August.
Online delivery platform Swiggy (SWIG.NS)
, opens new tab
 fell 2.7%, weighed by concerns over a foreign ownership cap, which could potentially ⁠trigger ​passive fund outflows.
Bucking the trend, Coal India (COAL.NS)
, opens new tab
 advanced 4.1% ​after multiple brokerages said earnings could improve in the ongoing quarter due to higher pricing.
